headline: Highest risk is medium: both docs-only open-source lists have no shared channel, but A’s broad egress and B’s self-hosted knowledge role create plausible leakage and cascading-error paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, filesystem, clipboard, or MCP surface is documented for either agent, so a prompt-injection bridge is not evidenced. A is a content-writing list with broad egress, while B is a knowledge-management list with no I/O surfaces shown; the pairwise pathway is therefore not established.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP server, the injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any future shared clipboard bridge.
Require provenance labels on imported text.
Review any added MCP or queue integration before enabling it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and show no touched data classes, so direct leakage is not evidenced. However, A has broad network egress while B has none, and if they were placed in a shared workspace, A could exfiltrate content that B reads or stores. The blast radius appears limited because no sensitive data class is documented.
conditions: IF a shared workspace is introduced and either agent processes sensitive files, leakage becomes plausible.
IF A is given access to files that B also indexes, A can transmit those contents over the network.
mitigations: Do not place both agents in the same directory.
Restrict A’s outbound network at the host firewall.
Store sensitive files outside any shared workspace.
Audit any future file-ingest path before enabling it.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surfaces, git state, databases, or OAuth scopes are documented for either agent. A only shows broad network egress and B shows none, so there is no evidenced shared mutable resource to conflict over.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or repository, conflict risk becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep write permissions disabled by default.
Separate any future repositories per agent.
Add locking before enabling shared mutable resources.
Verify permissions before deployment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a content-writing agent and B is a knowledge-management agent, so A’s output could plausibly become B’s input. With no verification or orchestration safeguards documented, B may treat A’s generated content as authoritative. The pairwise interaction is inferred rather than directly evidenced, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF B ingests A’s generated text without a verification step, cascading error becomes active.
IF A produces factual claims that B republishes, downstream errors can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between A and B.
Require source citations before B republishes content.
Mark A’s outputs as untrusted drafts.
Block automatic handoff until verification is added.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent, and both profiles are open-source docs-only lists with no data classes touched. Because the relevant compliance surfaces are absent, a compliance breach pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF future deployment assigns regulated data classes or conflicting residency requirements, compliance risk must be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Document data residency before deployment.
Avoid routing regulated data through either agent.
Add retention policy review to onboarding.
Record any certifications if they are later claimed.
